questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?

options.text: Front tires need a tread depth of at least 4/32 inch.
Rear tires need a tread depth of at least 2/32 inch.
Use a gauge to check that each tire has enough tread.

questions.explanation: In winter, your tires need good tread. Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread depth. Rear tires need at least 2/32 inch. Use a gauge to check the tread on all tires. Do not deflate your tires.

questions.question: What two things tell you when to shift to a higher gear?

options.text: Oil pressure and air brake pressure.

questions.explanation: Two things determine when to shift up. First is engine speed (rpm). Check your vehicle manual for the correct rpm range and shift up when you reach the top. Second is road speed (mph). Learn which speeds work for each gear, watch your speedometer, and shift up as needed.

questions.question: What does a driver need to accept a package of hazardous materials, unless it is clearly unsafe?
questions.explanation: When a shipper packages hazardous materials, they certify that it follows the rules. You can accept the package based on the shipper's certification, unless the package is clearly unsafe or does not follow the rules.

questions.question: What letters appear on shipping papers and packages for reportable quantities?
questions.explanation: When a substance is shipped in a reportable quantity, the shipper must mark it with the letters "RQ" on the shipping papers and package.

questions.question: When it is hard for others to see your vehicle at dawn or dusk, what should you do?

options.text: Wave your arm out the window.

questions.explanation: When visibility is low, turn on your headlights to low beam. If you cannot see others clearly, they probably cannot see you either.

questions.question: When inspecting a coupling, what should you check under the trailer?

options.text: Detach the jaws from around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking lever is in the "emergency" position.
Look into the back of the fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the back of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: Go under the trailer and look into the back of the fifth wheel. Make sure the fifth wheel jaws are locked around the kingpin shank.

questions.question: What should you use when parked on the side of the road?
questions.explanation: Always turn on your four-way emergency flashers when you park on the side of the road. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: When a tire goes flat with a loud bang, when will the truck be affected?

options.text: Only if the flat tire is near the front.
Only if the truck is carrying a load.

questions.explanation: There is usually a delay of a few seconds between the sound of a tire failing and when the truck is affected. Because of this delay, you might think the sound came from another vehicle.

questions.question: What is the minimum size for hazardous materials placards?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be at least 10 and three-quarter inches square.

questions.question: What should you do with manhole covers when driving?
questions.explanation: Always check your vehicle before driving. Never drive a tank vehicle with open valves or manhole covers.

questions.question: Before entering a curve, you should:
questions.explanation: Always shift to a lower gear before entering a curve. Slowing down before the curve helps you control your vehicle better while turning.

questions.question: You should always be able to stop within:

options.text: The distance you can see ahead on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance you can see ahead on the road.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must be able to stop within the area you can see ahead. Slow down whenever you cannot see far down the road.

questions.question: To prevent a rollover, a driver should:
questions.explanation: Keep your vehicle's center of gravity low by loading cargo as close to the ground as possible. This helps prevent rollovers when turning.

questions.question: On a shipping paper, if the letter "G" appears in Column 1, what else must appear?

options.text: The technical name of the hazardous material.
The type of packaging for the hazardous material.
The date the product was packed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The technical name of the hazardous material.
questions.explanation: If "G" (meaning "Generic") appears in Column 1, you must also list the technical name of the hazardous material.

questions.question: If a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, how can you tell them apart?

options.text: Non-hazardous materials are written in pencil.
Hazardous materials are written in red ink.
Hazardous materials are written in larger print.

questions.explanation: Hazardous materials must be shown differently than non-hazardous materials. They can be listed first, highlighted in a contrasting color, or marked with an "X" in a column titled "HM."

questions.question: How long must shippers keep a copy of shipping papers?
questions.explanation: Shippers must keep a copy of hazardous materials shipping papers for at least two years after the materials are picked up by the first carrier. For hazardous waste, the time increases to three years.

questions.question: Skids caused by speeding up can usually be fixed by:
questions.explanation: Release the accelerator pedal to correct a skid caused by speeding up. If you are on a very slippery surface, you may also need to push in the clutch.

questions.question: Combination vehicles need more road space than other commercial vehicles because they are longer and they:

options.text: Need more space to turn and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need more space to turn and stop.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more space because they are longer and require more room to turn and stop. Managing space properly is very important when driving a combination vehicle.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.
Roll down your window to listen for a train.
Never try to race a train across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never try to race a train across the tracks.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a railroad crossing. You may not hear a train, and signals may not always warn you. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: Rollovers are most likely to happen when:
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn too fast. Always slow down before entering turns and curves, especially when carrying a full load.
